messages:
Alex: Quick idea - introduce a 'lateral throttle' (rate-sink) that diverts excess noisy-tenant requests into a degradable execution path instead of hard rejects. Main goals: soak bursts, keep P99 fairly stable, avoid sudden client errors. Thoughts? :thinking:
Maya: Love the idea. How is this different from our current soft-shed? Is sink admission reversible or sticky?
Devon: Interface note: ingress should hand out a short-lived sink_token when diverting. Downstream runtime consumes token and chooses degraded model/queue semantics. If downstream doesn't understand the token, ingress should fail fast with 503 so we don't silently process. Proposed header: `X-Rate-Sink: admit=true;token=abc123;mode=degraded`.
Lina: Billing/telemetry: sunk requests must be metered separately and billed at lower unit price. Add trace tag `sink=true` and a metric `sink_units`. Also need a console panel.
Samir: Abuse risk: attackers could craft traffic to be sunk and then use that to probe degraded models or bypass quotas. We need per-tenant sink_quota, an abuse_score cutoff, and a leak-rate limiter on sink admits.
Alex: Implementation knobs sketch: per-tenant sink_capacity, global sink_leaky_bucket, sink_ttl ~5s. Admitted sink requests get degraded model (smaller model/less tokens) and relaxed latency targets. Rollout behind feature flag.
Maya: Failure semantics: if a sinked request times out, should clients retry to ingress? I'd prefer surfacing `retryable=false` in the sink response to avoid thundering.
Devon: Agree. Also propose SinkAdmission proto: `admit: bool`, `token: string`, `mode: "degraded"|"queue"`, `retryable: bool`. Ingress SDK will enforce TTL and attach token.
Lina: Policy exemptions: dedicated/reserved tenants and compliance-bound customers must be exempt from sinking. Need policy gate that checks `tenant_tier` and `compliance_flags`.
Samir: Telemetry / alerts: `sink_wait_ms` histogram, `sink_admit_rate`, `sink_queue_depth`. Alert if queue depth > threshold for N minutes. Also track `sink_eject_reason` tags for postmortems.
Alex: Cost control: impose a small budget drain while in sink so it isn't free. Maybe a per-sink_penalty that consumes tenant budget over time. Also keep sink processing cheaper per-token to reflect degraded service.
Maya: I'll run synthetic workloads to measure fairness delta and cost impact. Need a model-sim for degraded path.
Devon: I'll add trace hooks and runtime flag to accept sink_token and pick degraded kernels. Also will ensure services unaware of sink_token decline explicitly.
Samir: I'll draft an RFC covering proto, telemetry keys, abuse mitigations, rollout plan and rollback gates. Include simulator and safety thresholds.
Alex: Great. Please include expected QPS, target P99 impact, and cost model for degraded path. Assign owners in RFC.
Maya: I'll own the simulation and start a runbook. Devon will pair on instrumentation.
Lina: I'll own billing/console changes and prepare the SKU proposal.
Alex: Thanks all. RFC -> sim -> beta behind flag. Closing thread.
